text:
maria.escobar: Hey - customer ACME reports weird partial SSE payloads when clients reconnect through their gRPC-web gateway. They see duplicate prefix tokens and sometimes a truncated final event.

maria.escobar: Symptoms: client gets initial events, connection drops, client reconnects, then next stream contains a repeat of the last 1-2 events (duplicate) and occasionally the final event is cut mid-chunk. Billing showed two short streams counted separately.

devon: Do we know the gateway stack? Envoy in front of gRPC-web or a custom proxy?

maria.escobar: They said: gRPC-web -> custom node gateway -> our HTTP/2 edge. Gateway does HTTP/1.1 to the browser, translates to HTTP/2 upstream.

sam: Ok so middle translator. This screams chunk boundary / KV cache / prefix handling bug. Any request/response headers or repro curl?

maria.escobar: Provided repro:
```bash
# repro (sanitized token)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Client: acme-browser" \\n  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-xl'
```
They say after ~30s the gateway closes and client reconnects with Last-Event-ID set.

jamie: Do we preserve Last-Event-ID semantics? Our runtime appends KV cache frames and replays from cached prefix. If gateway terminates the TCP but not the HTTP/2 stream properly we could be replaying a partial in-memory prefix.

sam: Can we see logs from their connection path? Specifically we need the upstream request id, bytes_sent/received, and any reset reason (RST_STREAM or GOAWAY).

maria.escobar: They attached partial logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-01T12:01:23Z] gateway: client disconnect, id=cid-42, reason=idle_timeout
[2026-03-01T12:01:23Z] gateway: translate->upstream id=up-9001: started h2 stream
[2026-03-01T12:01:23Z] upstream=api.redwood: RST_STREAM received, code=NO_ERROR\\n[2026-03-01T12:01:23Z] gateway: client reconnect with Last-Event-ID=event-789
[2026-03-01T12:01:23Z] translate->upstream id=up-9002: resumed h2 stream with Range:start=event-789
[2026-03-01T12:01:24Z] upstream=api.redwood: wrote cached prefix bytes=2048
[2026-03-01T12:01:24Z] upstream=api.redwood: wrote delta bytes=128
[2026-03-01T12:01:24Z] upstream=api.redwood: RST_STREAM code=INTERNAL_ERROR
```

devon: Interesting: gateway sends RST_STREAM NO_ERROR on the first disconnect, then our upstream emits INTERNAL_ERROR on the replay. That could result in the gateway buffering partial chunks and re-emitting prefix bytes combined with the replayed prefix from our cache -> duplicates.

jamie: Also note the gateway translates between HTTP/1.1 SSE and HTTP/2 frames. Some gateways implement chunked encoding framing differently. If they buffer until a CRLF boundary, a mid-chunk RST could leave an incomplete event in their buffer that is emitted on reconnect. Combined with our KV prefix replay, duplicates appear.

sam: Repro plan for support: ask customer to switch the gateway to passthrough mode (no buffering) or enable the gateway's "flush-on-chunk" option. If they can't, ask them to test connecting directly to our edge (bypass gateway) to confirm whether problem disappears.

maria.escobar: They tried direct connect to our edge and issue disappears. So it's definitely the intermediary. But they need a mitigation because they must use the gateway for auth and other transforms.

devon: Short-term: add idempotency hints. If they set Last-Event-ID, our runtime can annotate events with a monotonic event-seq header and we could suppress events <= last seen on reconnect. But we have to be careful: some clients rely on precise order. Would be an opt-in header like X-Redwood-Event-Seq.

jamie: That helps but won't address partial truncation mid-event. For truncate, we should ensure we never send partial event markers in cache replay — only complete SSE event blocks. Our KV cache should track event boundaries. If cache returned incomplete event, it should wait to flush until the event completes or mark as continued and avoid replaying the incomplete part on reconnect.

eng-runtime: Adding notes: we currently cache tokenized outputs and stream raw byte chunks to the HTTP layer. We don't maintain SSE event boundaries in the cache. This is by design for throughput, but it makes replay ambiguous when intermediaries chop streams mid-event.

eng-runtime: Proposed: 1) When streaming SSE, also emit and cache explicit "event-boundary" markers (lightweight framing). 2) On reconnect with Last-Event-ID, replay from the last completed marker. 3) Expose opt-in header X-Redwood-SSE-Atomic to preserve event granularity.

sam: For support reply: provide clear repro steps (direct vs via gateway), ask for gateway config (buffer size, idle timeout, streaming translation mode), and offer the opt-in headers workaround while eng evaluates event-boundary caching. Also flag billing: duplicated streams may cause double short-charge. We should offer to credit duplicated token charges for impacted windows.

maria.escobar: I'll draft a support message: repro instructions, suggested gateway toggles (flush-on-chunk / disable buffering), opt-in header X-Redwood-SSE-Atomic mention, and offer billing credit while engineering investigates.

devon: +1. Also capture examples of truncated event payloads (hex/byte offsets) if they can provide tcpdump from the gateway to pinpoint cut points.

maria.escobar: Filed to customer. Escalating to eng-runtime for design: please track as SR-STREAM-392 and advise ETA on opt-in event-boundary caching.

ops-bot: Incident created: SR-STREAM-392, priority=P2, owner=eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: Acknowledged. We'll review logs and determine perf impact. Likely short-term patch + opt-in header within 2 sprints.

maria.escobar: Thanks team! I'll keep support thread updated and confirm billing credit once applied.
